messages:
Priya: Quick UX nit — audit search currently shows timestamps in UTC but the control says "Timezone: local (UTC)" which is confusing. Can we make the timezone affordance clearer and expose a selector in the search panel? Also needs keyboard support.

Lina: +1. Right now the only hint is tiny text under the results. Suggestion: show a compact pill: "Times shown: Pacific (UTC-7) ▾" that opens a timezone menu. If space is tight, make it part of the search header.

Sam: Accessibility note: the control should have an aria-label like "Time zone selector, currently Pacific Time (UTC-7)" and the selected value must be announced when focused. Also ensure the date picker and timezone selector's focus order is logical (tz before range).

Anna: Copy tweak idea: change "Timestamps in UTC" to "Times shown" with a secondary line: "Stored in: eu-west-1 (for this log)" when applicable. People confuse display timezone vs storage region.

Priya: Important edge-case: when people pick a date range in the UI we convert to UTC for the backend. That can shift the day boundary and cause missing events (esp for midnight-heavy cron jobs). We should add helper text in the date picker: "Selecting dates uses the displayed timezone (Pacific, UTC-7). Backend stores UTC, conversions shown above." Example under the picker might help.

Sam: Agree. Also propose adding a per-row timestamp tooltip showing both values: "03/10/2026 00:15 PDT (UTC 2026-03-10 07:15)". Screenreaders should get a shortened accessible label: "Mar 10 12:15 AM Pacific, 07:15 UTC".

Anna: For exports, current CSV header uses "Timestamp (UTC)" even when users selected a different timezone. Suggest we add an option in export modal: "Export timestamps as: [Account timezone / Browser timezone / UTC]" and default to Account timezone. Copy for the checkbox: "Export in selected timezone (recommended for local review)".

Priya: Another small product question: should default be Account timezone or Browser local? For orgs, Account makes more sense for consistency. Thoughts?

Lina: Account timezone default is preferable for shared dashboards. Browser local is surprising in team contexts. +1 for Account.

Sam: Implementation nit: backend stores and indexes everything in UTC. When accepting a date range from UI we should include the timezone offset in the query (e.g., "from=2026-03-10T00:00-07:00"). That will remove ambiguity. I'll add the param to the search API.

Priya: UX copy proposal coming from my end. Short versions:
- Option A: "Times shown: Pacific (UTC-7) — change" (compact)
- Option B: "Displaying times in: Pacific Time (UTC-7). Click to change or learn more."

Anna: For the small "learn more" modal, add a short example and a mini diagram: select Mar 10 00:00 in PST -> backend query uses Mar 10 07:00 UTC. Keep it 2 sentences max.

Sam: Accessibility checklist I'll follow:
- timezone selector aria-label
- focus order (tz -> date range -> submit)
- visible focus ring on pill/button
- export modal accessible radio group for timezone choices

AuditBot: Note: query-id 7b9f2a returned 3 hits flagged as "timestamp-mismatch" in last 24h; reason: user submitted end-of-day in local tz which mapped to previous day in UTC.

Priya: Thanks — I'll drop Figma mockups for Option A/B in #design and tag you all. Unless any objections, we'll default to Account timezone and add the small "Stored in: <region>" badge for exports.

Lina: No objections. Small follow-up: can we add a11y text for the region badge: "Stored in region eu-west-1" so screenreaders don't skip it?

Sam: Yep, I'll include aria-hidden=false and an aria-label.

Anna: One last copy nit: replace "Why different?" with "Why do displayed times differ from stored times?" in the help link — clearer for search.

Priya: Perfect. I'll iterate on copy + mock and post back with screenshots. :thumbsup:
